passages.text: That each person’s soul, in accordance with its preconceptions, portrays forms of demons, and that the so-called gods do not appear, is clear from the fact that they do not appear to Jews. But someone will say, “How, then, do they deliver oracles that foretell the future?” This too is false. Yet grant that it is true: does that make such a thing a god? For something is not a god merely because it foretells the future. Python mediums also foretell the future, but when we adjure them as demons, they are driven away. But someone will say, “They prescribe treatments for some people.” That is false. Yet grant that this is so: does that make such a thing a god? Physicians also heal many people, and they are not gods. “But,” someone says, “physicians do not invariably heal those for whom they care, whereas these both deliver an oracle and heal.” Demons, however, know the remedies truly suited to each particular ailment. Consequently, they are knowledgeable physicians, capable of healing—and that in cases capable of being healed by human beings. But they are also divinatory beings and know when each person will recover spontaneously; at that moment they prescribe the treatments, so that they may claim the credit for themselves.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in accordance with its preconceptions
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρός with the accusative here indicates correspondence to each soul’s prior conceptions, which determine the forms it portrays.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Python mediums
lexical_decisions.rationale: The term denotes persons or agencies associated with a Python spirit and practicing divination; alternatives include “Python spirits” and “those possessed by Python.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δεδόσθω δὲ ἀλήθειαν εἶναι, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Yet grant that it is true: does that make such a thing a god?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Although the final clause can be punctuated as a statement, the following denial shows that it functions rhetorically: even genuine prediction would not establish divinity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων ἰαθῆναι δυνάμενα
lexical_decisions.chosen: and that in cases capable of being healed by human beings
lexical_decisions.rationale: The emphatic καὶ ταῦτα limits or qualifies the preceding ability: the ailments in question are also within the scope of human medicine. A more literal alternative is “and these being things capable of being healed by humans.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: so that they may claim the credit for themselves
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally, they seek to “inscribe” themselves upon the cure, idiomatically attaching their own name or credit to it.

source_issues.issue: The printed text shifts to neuter plural participial forms after the masculine subjects οἱ δαίμονες and ἰατροὶ ... δυνάμενοι. This may be an anacoluthon or may imply the neuter δαιμόνια. English can preserve the demons as the semantic subject without resolving the morphological shift.

passages.text: For why do they announce healings by oracle only after a long time? Why, if they can do everything, do they not bring about healing without an offering? Why do they prescribe treatments for some who pray, but sometimes deliver no oracle to others who are even more closely connected with them? It is in this way: whenever a spontaneous recovery is about to occur, they make a promise so that they may claim the credit for themselves. Others fell ill and prayed, and when they recovered spontaneously, they credited those whom they had invoked and made votive offerings. Those, however, for whom matters turned out otherwise after prayer cannot dedicate their failures. Yet if the relatives of the dead, or some of those people themselves, were to compile the failures, you would find the failures more numerous than the successes. But no one who is already prepossessed in their favor wants to expose the case against them, being ashamed or afraid. On the contrary, they join in concealing their well-attested absurdities.

lexical_decisions.chosen: without an offering
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantivized infinitive refers to presenting something, naturally an offering in this cultic context; “without presenting anything” is the more literal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: who are even more closely connected with them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The comparative describes a closer relationship or affiliation, though whether familial, cultic, or generally intimate is not specified.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἱ μέντοι γε μετὰ εὐχὴν διαφωνήσαντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: Those, however, for whom matters turned out otherwise after prayer
lexical_decisions.rationale: διαφωνέω literally concerns disagreement or discrepancy; here it contrasts unsuccessful outcomes with the reported recoveries.

lexical_decisions.chosen: were to compile the failures
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb can mean investigate or examine together; “compile” fits the comparison between the total numbers of failures and successes. “Jointly investigate the failures” remains possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: already prepossessed in their favor
lexical_decisions.rationale: The perfect participle describes someone whose judgment has already been captured or prejudiced by them; “previously taken in by them” is an alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: their well-attested absurdities
lexical_decisions.rationale: πιστά can mean trustworthy, credible, or firmly established. Here it characterizes the ἀτοπήματα as reliable evidence of their absurd conduct, not as conduct worthy of trust.

source_issues.issue: The print has the unassimilated compound spelling συνκρύβουσιν where συγκρύβουσιν would be the standard assimilated form. The sense “conceal together” or “join in concealing” remains clear.

passages.text: How many also falsely claim that oracles were given and that healings were accomplished by them, and confirm these claims with oaths? How many have hired themselves out for pay, undertaking through various contrivances to suffer some ailment and advertising it as such; then, after being restored from their ailment by counteraction, they say that the treatment had been prescribed by oracle, so that they may credit the insensible object of worship? How many of them were established from the outset by magical art, so that it might ὑνερπολῇ and deliver oracles? And yet, after a long time, these too failed. How many now practice sorcery because they want to strengthen such things? Nevertheless, something is not a god merely because it can foretell the future or bring healing.

lexical_decisions.chosen: have hired themselves out for pay
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expression describes placing oneself at another’s disposal in return for payment.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: δι’ ἐνίων ἐπινοιῶν πάσχειν τινὰ ἀναδεξάμενοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: undertaking through various contrivances to suffer some ailment
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπίνοιαι are devised schemes or contrivances, while ἀναδέχομαι indicates undertaking or assuming the staged affliction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after being restored from their ailment by counteraction
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀντιπάθεια denotes an opposing or counteracting influence, possibly a treatment by contraries; the source does not specify its mechanism.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so that they may credit the insensible object of worship
lexical_decisions.rationale: As in 9.16, ἐπιγράφω concerns attaching a name or credit. The object of worship is characterized as without perception or sensation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: How many of them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter plural may refer to the objects of worship just mentioned or more generally to such cultic phenomena; the English leaves the referent open.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ὅμως μακρῷ χρόνῳ καὶ ταῦτα διεφώνησεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: And yet, after a long time, these too failed
lexical_decisions.rationale: διαφωνέω here indicates that the promised or manufactured results ceased to agree with the claims and proved unsuccessful; “turned out otherwise” is an alternative.

source_issues.issue: The image-checked print clearly reads ὑνερπολῇ, but no defensible lexical sense or regular formation can be established for that supplied form. It has therefore been retained untranslated rather than silently replaced. The conjecture ὑπερπολῇ could mean “gain ascendancy” or “flourish,” but that wording is not the selected edition’s reading and has not been imported into the translation.

passages.text: For God can do everything. He is good and just, showing patience toward everyone now, so that those who are willing may regret the evils they have committed and live accordingly, and, on the day when everything is judged, receive what they deserve. Therefore begin now, obeying God, the cause of good knowledge, to oppose your evil desires and thoughts, so that you may recover for yourselves the original saving religion handed down to humanity. In this way good things will immediately spring up for you; once you have received them, you will thereafter leave behind your experience of evils. But give thanks to the one who gave them, reigning forever with the King of Peace over the inexpressible good things. In the present, after washing yourselves in an ever-flowing river or spring, or indeed even in the sea, with the thrice-blessed invocation, you will be able not only to drive away the spirits lurking in your innermost recesses, but also—if you yourselves no longer sin and believe God without wavering—to drive out other people’s evil spirits and fierce demons, together with their dreadful afflictions. Sometimes, however, they will flee when you merely yield. For they recognize those who have given themselves to God, and therefore, showing them honor, they flee in fear. Just yesterday you saw how, when after the discourse I undertook to pray for those who were suffering, the afflictions themselves cried aloud out of respect for the religion, unable to endure even a short time.

lexical_decisions.chosen: may regret
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb denotes regret or a change of concern regarding the evils committed. It is kept distinct from the μετανοέω terminology governed by the reorientation policy.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and live accordingly
lexical_decisions.rationale: πολιτεύομαι concerns conducting one’s life. “Accordingly” expresses the contextual connection with regret without adding a new intensifier; “conduct their lives” is the more formally literal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: obeying God, the cause of good knowledge
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative αἰτίᾳ can stand in apposition to θεῷ, identifying God as the cause of good knowledge. Another possible attachment is “for the sake of good knowledge, obeying God.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν πρώτην τῇ ἀνθρωπότητι παραδοθεῖσαν σωτήριον θρησκείαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the original saving religion handed down to humanity
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρώτην characterizes the religion as first or original, while σωτήριον describes it as saving. The wording preserves the author’s historical claim without harmonization.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἅτινα λαβόντες πεῖραν τῶν κακῶν τοῦ λοιποῦ καταλείψετε
lexical_decisions.chosen: once you have received them, you will thereafter leave behind your experience of evils
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἅτινα is taken as the object of λαβόντες, while πεῖραν is the object of καταλείψετε and τῶν κακῶν depends on πεῖραν. This avoids changing the case relationships.

lexical_decisions.chosen: with the thrice-blessed invocation
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπονομασία can mean naming, designation, or invocation. In the washing context, “invocation” best conveys an enacted naming formula without supplying its unquoted words.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the spirits lurking in your innermost recesses
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνδομυχέω depicts dwelling or hiding deep within, preserving the spatial image.

lexical_decisions.chosen: when you merely yield
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive absolute uses ἐνδίδωμι in its intransitive sense “yield” or “give way.” In context this may mean yielding oneself to God, as the following clause explains; “when you merely permit it” is another possible sense.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the afflictions themselves cried aloud
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter plural subject takes a singular verb, a normal Greek construction. The personification or identification of the afflictions with their spiritual agents is preserved rather than explained away.

passages.text: Therefore, do not suppose that because we are of another nature, we do not fear demons. For we are of the same nature as you, though not of the same religion. Consequently, although we are not merely a little but altogether superior to you, we do not begrudge your becoming the same; on the contrary, we recommend it, knowing that all these beings, without understanding, esteem and fear those who have become closely allied with God.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς γὰρ αὐτῆς ὑμῖν ἐσμὲν φύσεως, ἀλλ᾽ οὐ θρησκείας
lexical_decisions.chosen: For we are of the same nature as you, though not of the same religion
lexical_decisions.rationale: The second genitive is elliptical, contrasting shared human nature with differing religion or worship.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ πολύ, ἀλλὰ τὸ πᾶν κρείττονες
lexical_decisions.chosen: not merely a little but altogether superior
lexical_decisions.rationale: The contrast emphatically denies a small degree of superiority and asserts it comprehensively; “superior in every respect” is a possible stronger English formulation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ὑμᾶς τοιούτους γενέσθαι οὐ φθονοῦμεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: we do not begrudge your becoming the same
lexical_decisions.rationale: τοιούτους refers to becoming people of the same religious standing just described, while φθονέω means begrudge or envy another’s acquisition of it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: those who have become closely allied with God
lexical_decisions.rationale: προσοικειόω denotes being brought into close relationship or affinity. Alternatives include “those made God’s own” and “those who have drawn near to God.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ταῦτα πάντα ἀγνώστως προτιμᾷ καὶ φοβεῖται
lexical_decisions.chosen: all these beings, without understanding, esteem and fear
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter plural collectively refers to the demonic beings under discussion and therefore takes singular Greek verbs. ἀγνώστως may mean “unknowingly,” “without understanding,” or “in an inexplicable manner”; the chosen wording allows them to recognize God’s people, as stated previously, without necessarily understanding the reason for their authority.
